summary: Round 2. Re-checked only the NEW or CHANGED claims (24 of them); round 1's 57 claims / 50 confirmations stand and were not re-verified. All seven substantive new arguments hold: OverviewWalSize really does call pg_ls_waldir() on every verbose tick, the recorder really does run every recordable view's query each tick, printStatHeader really does gate on Aligned, the procpidstat no-data notice really is ReportType-gated, doc/release-notes/ really stops at v0.9.0 and v0.9.0.md really documents a hotkey break in prose, the fixture role really is the superuser `postgres`, and ReportType really is both a tar-entry filter and a view-map key. Seven defects found, none critical: one testing-strategy gap (the pg_monitor-only role the SET ROLE tests need does not exist anywhere and nothing says who creates it), one mislocated acceptance criterion, two round-1 fixes that were only half-applied, one new off-by-one introduced by a round-1 fix, one over-strong wording in Decision 15, and one claim that pgcenter's tree cannot support either way.

findings.claim: Testing Strategy (:334-338), Task 1 (:467) and Task 3 (:498-499): privilege behaviour is proven "Using `SET ROLE` against the fixture cluster" — the archiver query and the verbose backlog aggregate run "under a role holding only `pg_monitor`", and the archiver query fails without it.
findings.reality: Mechanically possible but nothing in the tree provides the role. `internal/postgres/testing.go:6-7,:41` connects as user `postgres` (trust auth, db `pgcenter_fixtures`) — a superuser — and `DB.Conn` is a single `*pgx.Conn` (internal/postgres/postgres.go:22-26) with an `Exec` wrapper (:119-121), so `CREATE ROLE`/`SET ROLE`/`RESET ROLE` do work on that session. But: grep over the whole repo finds ZERO occurrences of `SET ROLE`, `CREATE ROLE` or `GRANT` in any .go file — no precedent to copy. The `pg_monitor`-only role does not exist in the fixture image, and the Risks table (:430) states the image is deliberately NOT changed, so the test itself must create it. Neither Task 1 nor Task 3 says so, names the role, or addresses that role creation is a cluster-wide persistent side effect (a second run of the suite against the same container hits `role already exists` unless the test is written idempotently, and a missing `RESET ROLE` would leak the demoted role into every later query on that connection).
findings.source: 017-feat-wal-archiver-tech-spec.md, Testing Strategy ("Privilege behaviour is tested, not asserted"), Task 1 Description/Verify, Task 3 Verify, Acceptance Criteria :453-455
findings.fix: State in Task 1 (and reference from Task 3) that the test creates its own role — e.g. `DROP ROLE IF EXISTS pgcenter_test_monitor; CREATE ROLE pgcenter_test_monitor IN ROLE pg_monitor;` via `db.Exec`, then `SET ROLE` / `RESET ROLE` with a `t.Cleanup` that drops it — and note that the negative direction needs a second role with no `pg_monitor` membership. Without this the executor has no precedent in the tree to imitate.

findings.claim: Acceptance Criteria :456: "The two comments in `internal/stat/` that state `pg_ls_dir` requires 'pg_monitor/superuser' are corrected".
findings.reality: The pair Task 3 describes (wrong privilege requirement AND the path-swallowing justification) is `internal/query/overview.go:97-99` ("pg_ls_dir requires pg_monitor/superuser; this query MUST be run as its OWN QueryRow ... The raw error (containing the path) must never be surfaced") and `internal/stat/postgres.go:288-290` ("pg_ls_dir requires pg_monitor/superuser ... The raw error (which contains a filesystem path) is deliberately swallowed"). Both exist and say exactly what the spec says they say — but only ONE of them is in `internal/stat/`; the other is in `internal/query/`. An executor grepping `internal/stat/` for the criterion finds a single hit and may "complete" it by also editing the unrelated struct-field comment at internal/stat/postgres.go:83-84.
findings.source: 017-feat-wal-archiver-tech-spec.md, Acceptance Criteria (last bullet); cross-checked against Task 3 Description and Files to modify
findings.fix: Reword to "The two comments — `internal/query/overview.go:97-99` and `internal/stat/postgres.go:288-290` — that state `pg_ls_dir` requires pg_monitor/superuser are corrected". Task 3's Files to modify already lists both files, so only the criterion's wording is wrong.

findings.claim: Task 3 scopes the comment corrections to "Two existing comments" (plus the four files it lists as Files to modify).
findings.reality: Two MORE comments in the same files carry the same false premise and are not named anywhere: `internal/query/overview_test.go:124-126` — "pg_ls_dir, which requires pg_monitor/superuser. On the test clusters the fixtures role has access" — and `internal/stat/postgres_test.go:224` — "the fixtures role has pg_monitor, so the OWN-QueryRow aggregate must run". The fixtures role is the superuser `postgres` (internal/postgres/testing.go), not a pg_monitor member; these comments are exactly the wrong-assumption trail the criterion at :456 exists to erase, and both files are already in Task 3's Files to modify.
findings.fix: Say "four comments — two in the source files and two in their tests", or add a sentence to Task 3 that the test comments must stop claiming the fixtures role has pg_monitor when it is in fact the superuser.

findings.claim: Decision 15: "`report -W a` over an archive containing no `archiver` entries prints an empty output — no rows and no header — and exits 0."
findings.reality: The load-bearing half is confirmed: `printStatHeader` (report/report.go:559-563) returns early on `printedNum < repeatHeaderAfter || !v.Aligned`; `Aligned` is set only in `formatStatSample` (report/report.go:527-538), whose sole call site is report/report.go:363 — inside the data branch, after the first-sample discard; and the no-data notice at report/report.go:391 is gated on `!anyDataPrinted && config.ReportType == "procpidstat"`. But the output is never literally empty: `RunMain` calls `printReportHeader` at report/report.go:63 before `doReport`, which unconditionally prints three INFO lines ("INFO: reading from …", "INFO: report …", "INFO: start from: …, to: …").
findings.fix: Phrase it as "prints the usual three INFO header lines and nothing else — no column header, no rows — and exits 0", so a QA step that greps for empty stdout is not written against a false expectation.

findings.claim: Decision 2 (rewritten in round 1): "the TUI calls `calculateDelta` directly (`internal/stat/stat.go:441`)".
findings.reality: Off by one in the opposite direction: internal/stat/stat.go:439 is the comment `// Compare previous and current Postgres stats snapshots and calculate delta.`, the `calculateDelta(...)` call is at :440, and :441 is `if err != nil {`. (Round 1's own report said comment :440 / call :441 — that was itself off by one, and the correction propagated the wrong number into the spec.) The other two references in the same sentence are exact: `report/report.go:505` is the `stat.Compare(...)` call inside `countDiff`, and `internal/stat/postgres.go:575-577` is the `Compare` wrapper that delegates to `calculateDelta`. Architecture's `internal/stat/postgres.go:589-597` for the `{0,0}` short-circuit is also exact.

findings.claim: Decision 12 still reads: "`report/report.go:315-320` discards the first sample unconditionally". Round 1 reported this line reference as fixed.
findings.reality: Not applied — the text is unchanged and still wrong. The discard is the block `if !prevStat.Valid || versionChanged {` at report/report.go:277, whose body reassigns prevMeta/prevStat/prevTs and ends with `continue` at :319. Lines 314-317 are `orderConfigured = false` / `v.OrderKey = seedOrderKey` / `v.OrderDesc = seedOrderDesc` inside the `if versionChanged` sub-branch, unrelated to the first-sample drop. "Unconditionally" is also loose: the drop is conditional on `!prevStat.Valid` or a recorded-version change.
findings.fix: Cite `report/report.go:277-319` (condition at :277, `continue` at :319) and say "the first sample is always dropped because it has no predecessor".

findings.claim: Task 6: "Add the `walNextView` cycle and its dispatch case, the two-item `W` menu with its keybinding, and **the two help-screen lines**." Round 1 reported the two-vs-three count as corrected to three.
findings.reality: Half-applied. Architecture (:41-43) now correctly says "three help-screen lines (`help.go`): the `w` entry moves out of the plain-switch line into its own `w,W` line, and the `Q`-does-not-reset caveat gains `archiver`" — and all three sites exist as described (top/help.go:14 `r,w  'r' replication, 'w' WAL,`; :19 the `j,J` model line; :45 `('Q' does not reset shared stats: pg_stat_io, bgwriter, wal)`). Task 6, the file the executor actually works from, still says two.
findings.fix: Change Task 6 to "three help-screen lines" to match Architecture, naming `help.go:45` so the `Q`-caveat edit is not dropped.

findings.claim: Task 1: the query comment must record that "PostgreSQL only ever reports names that passed its `VALID_XFN_CHARS` filter (hex plus `.history/.backup/.partial`), so debt [029] is not widened here".
findings.reality: The claim is correctly attributed to PostgreSQL's own behaviour ("its `VALID_XFN_CHARS` filter"), not to pgcenter — so it is not a mirage about this codebase. But pgcenter's tree cannot support it in either direction: `VALID_XFN_CHARS` appears nowhere in the repo outside this feature's own documents, and no vendored PostgreSQL source exists to check against. Debt [029] does exist (docs/tech-debt.md:47, "Row values reach the terminal unsanitised"). The feature's own security audit carries the citation the spec drops: `VALID_XFN_CHARS "0123456789ABCDEF.history.backup.partial"` in src/include/postmaster/pgarch.h, enforced by the `strspn` filter in `pgarch_readyXlog` (src/backend/postmaster/pgarch.c), with the fields written only by `pgstat_report_archiver`.
findings.fix: Carry the audit's citation into Task 1 (pgarch.h / pgarch_readyXlog), so the comment the executor writes points at a source a future reader can verify — the assertion is otherwise unfalsifiable from inside this repo.
